Maladaptive Strategies.value: I eat more than usual to distract myself or feel better
I go over and over the details of the event trying to make sense of it

Memory.value: The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me
My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.
The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me

Negative Appraisals.value: Somebody else would have stopped the event from happening
I have lost my connection to my community and culture
The person I have become is unrecognisable to me

vignette: Samantha is a 20-year-old South Eastern Asian female who recently experienced an assault during her service as a soldier. The traumatic event has profoundly impacted her life, leading to significant psychological distress and a series of maladaptive strategies she uses to cope. The assault occurred while Samantha was on patrol in a remote area. She vividly remembers the images from that day—the attacker’s face looming over hers, the sound of gunfire echoing through the night, and the sense of complete helplessness as the situation unfolded. These visual memories are so extreme that they feel almost surreal, making it difficult for her to accept that these events truly happened to her. Since then, Samantha has struggled with intense feelings of alienation from both herself and her community. She frequently overeats or focuses on other tasks to distract herself from intrusive thoughts about the assault. This pattern of overeating began shortly after the incident when she realized that food provided a temporary sense of comfort and distraction. Over time, this habit has become a significant part of her daily routine. The memory feels alien and distant, as if it belongs to someone else rather than Samantha herself. This disconnect makes it challenging for her to fully process what happened and integrate these experiences into her self-concept. She often finds herself overanalyzing the details of that night, trying to make sense of why she couldn’t prevent or stop the attack. Her thoughts are dominated by a belief that someone else—perhaps another soldier—would have had the strength or presence of mind to intervene. Her marriage has also been affected by these changes. Samantha feels increasingly disconnected from her husband and the community they once shared. She often finds herself questioning how she could ever return to the life she once knew, feeling like the person she has become is unrecognizable to her. This profound sense of loss leads her to engage in more frequent episodes of overeating or engaging in other avoidance behaviors. Samantha’s negative appraisals have reinforced these maladaptive strategies. Her belief that others would have prevented the event from happening fuels feelings of guilt and inadequacy, which she tries to alleviate through overeating and redirection. This cycle has intensified over time, leading her to rely more heavily on these coping mechanisms as a way to manage the overwhelming emotional distress. The assault’s visual memories continue to intrude upon her daily life, often triggering moments of intense anxiety and confusion. She finds herself constantly second-guessing her ability to cope with similar situations in the future, which further exacerbates her negative appraisals about her own resilience and strength. The memory feels so unreal that she often questions whether it truly happened, leading her to overanalyze every detail as a way of finding some semblance of control. Despite these challenges, Samantha finally sought help when her marriage began to suffer significantly from the strain of her coping mechanisms. She was certain that something had to change before her relationships and sense of self were irreparably damaged. What frightens her most is the possibility of never feeling like she can fully recover from this experience, while at the same time, she hopes for a way to reclaim a sense of normalcy and connection with herself and those around her. Samantha’s journey towards healing will require addressing both the maladaptive strategies that have become ingrained in her daily life and the negative appraisals that fuel them. She is determined to find a path forward where she can integrate her experiences without letting them define her, ultimately working towards a sense of wholeness and connection with herself and her community once again.
